spans.text: —Humanity has long envisioned artificial intelligence; through the past decades, if not centuries, one element of that vision remains unchanged: the imitation of man's very own nature.
Alas, how can one possibly tell if an AI's resolution stems from their analysis of data or their possession of a thinking, free will?
Inside her dimly lit, pungently coffee-scented lab, Persica lays in her seat, staring at the monitor in front.
...A new Doll? You don't seem to have ever mentioned such a bold plan to me.
Uhgh—?! Gosh, how do you walk with a cane without making any noise? You spooked the hell out of me!
Compared to the amount of distress you've caused me, I would consider that to be harmless payback.
I heard that you've conducted some experiments that I did not authorize. So now, I have to come down here personally for the details.
...Tsk.
That sentence leaves the usually preoccupied Persica visibly bewildered.
I thought we had reached a partnership through mutual trust.
"Mutual trust" is just a nice way of putting "staying in each other's lane".
I didn't inform you because the experiment has nothing to do with the performance of your products, it's just a small experiment of mine.
No experiment of yours is unrelated to us, besides, it is our job to support all your research.
Through his lenses, Havier's sharp gaze lands on the lab report sitting on the desktop.
But, I do see why you're reluctant to bring it up now.
I've only heard of this experiment's existence, but I did not expect the results to be... so jaw-dropping.
Experiment codename: “No Feeding”.
Test subjects: M4A1, AR15, M4 SOPMOD II, M16A1.
Test Sequence: 01
Result: Failure to complete the task.
